name: ColdSire
description: Premium cold-email inbox infrastructure — Google/Microsoft mailboxes from a pool mixed with real businesses, ~$6/mo per account, pitched at deliverability.

mentions.evidence: ~$15.6k MRR, 909 active subscriptions, ~$15.3k L30, ~$1.04M all-time, ~5,000 users claimed, founded May 2023, US. Last sync Oct 1, 2026.
mentions.indieAngle: Sell the boring dependency under a hot category (cold email) — inboxes, domains, warming — not another AI writer.

whyItPrints: Outbound teams don't want to babysit Google bans. Selling mailboxes as infra is unsexy and recurring; ~900 subs and $1M+ all-time say the pain is real (ethics/compliance vary by buyer — note the grey-hat adjacency).
whyThisMatters:
Outbound teams use ColdSire for the mailboxes behind cold email. You get Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 accounts. They say those accounts sit in a pool mixed with real businesses, and that cold email is capped at 15 percent of the pool. The rest aren't a farm of lookalike sending accounts. Each domain gets its own workspace and full admin access, so one domain's reputation stays off the others.

SPF, DKIM, and DMARC come preconfigured, along with forwarding. They say a mailbox is ready in about five minutes. It connects to Instantly and to SmartLead, so the sequencer you already use can send from these accounts. You can buy the .com domain in the same place. The company started in the US in May 2023. People who send cold email built it, for other people who send cold email.

They report more than 100,000 mailboxes set up and more than 40,000 domains under management, used by more than 5,000 companies and 500 agencies. You pay per mailbox. The purchase is an inbox that can still be delivered. The words in the email are a different tool.
